disposition: satisfied under the accepted per-operation authority model in Decisions 0042 and 0070
product_authority: ForgeWireLabs/repopact-core owns the RepoPact product and its complete governance boundary. Within Core, Decision 0042 assigns one normative implementation to each operation: Rust for migrated validation, dashboard, graph/analysis and typed work mutation; Python for expressly unmigrated Core operations. Workbench is a consumer and owns no competing governance semantics.

matrix.operation: Canonical repository validation and lifecycle/schema interpretation
matrix.authoritative_implementation: Rust repopact-validation and the repopact-engine validate operation.
callers_and_adapters: the final-validation paths of init, adopt, import-plan, doctor, takeover, and decision/policy creation
matrix.permitted_delegation: Python compatibility entry points send a versioned validate request to the matching Core engine and render its structured diagnostics.
matrix.non_authoritative_code: repopact.validate_repo.validate / repopact.legacy_validate are explicit compatibility-comparison code used by tests/conformance only; they are not the product validator and are never a fallback from migrated commands.

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Rust repopact-engine dashboard.write, backed by the Core repository/schema projection.
callers_and_adapters: Core Python workflows that refresh the derived dashboard
matrix.permitted_delegation: Callers request dashboard.write and check its canonical result; the Python writer is retained only as a test/reference utility for disposable conformance fixtures.

matrix.operation: Repository discovery, graph construction, graph queries and deterministic analysis
matrix.authoritative_implementation: Rust repopact-repository, repopact-graph, and repopact-analysis crates, exposed by typed repopact-engine graph/analyze operations.
matrix.permitted_delegation: Python and Workbench callers send typed requests/results to Core; presentation layers may filter/display returned facts but do not recompute graph meaning.

matrix.operation: Typed work-item creation, proposal, editing and lifecycle mutation
matrix.authoritative_implementation: Rust repopact-mutation and repopact-engine work.create/work.propose/work.amend_proposal; Workbench calls the same Core mutation crate through DesktopSession plan/apply.
matrix.permitted_delegation: Callers submit typed intent; Core plans, validates and applies it. No caller-provided arbitrary patch or Python lifecycle fallback is accepted.
tests: published Workbench Rust desktop-api mutation plan/apply integration tests

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core bootstrap/orchestration, explicitly unmigrated by Decision 0042.
matrix.permitted_delegation: Bootstrap creates the accepted seed structure; the shipped CLI preflights the Rust engine, uses Rust dashboard.write and uses Rust validate as the final repository-validity decision.

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core adoption/mapping workflow, explicitly unmigrated by Decision 0042.
matrix.permitted_delegation: Non-dry-run CLI preflights Rust validate/dashboard.write; the Python adopter maps source records; Rust validate decides final repository validity. Dry-run remains read-only.

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core legacy-plan import/mapping workflow, explicitly unmigrated by Decision 0042.
matrix.permitted_delegation: Non-dry-run preflights Rust validate/dashboard.write; Python maps incoming plans; the shipped CLI delegates final repository validity to Rust. Dry-run writes nothing.

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core doctor policy and repair selection, explicitly unmigrated by Decision 0042.
matrix.permitted_delegation: Fix preflights the required engine capabilities; graph facts are obtained from Rust where used; the CLI delegates final repository validity to Rust. Python-specific drift findings remain doctor findings, not replacement canonical validation.

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core retirement eligibility, archive/delete orchestration, and filesystem operation, explicitly unmigrated by Decision 0042.
matrix.permitted_delegation: Rust validate is required before retirement and after dashboard refresh. If the engine is unavailable or the pre-state is invalid, no retirement proceeds; Python owns the specific retirement policy.

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core template selection, ID allocation and document-authoring workflow, explicitly unmigrated by Decision 0042.
matrix.permitted_delegation: The shipped CLI requires validate/dashboard.write capabilities; Rust writes the derived dashboard and makes the final repository-validity decision.

matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core check_frozen_surface, explicitly unmigrated by Decision 0042; it evaluates the dedicated frozen-surface diff/acknowledgement rule, not general repository validity.
matrix.permitted_delegation: No Rust validation delegation is required for this separate read-only diff guard. It cannot silently acknowledge or rewrite frozen files.

matrix.operation: WI050 admission, approval, guard, authorization and enforcement
matrix.authoritative_implementation: Python Core admission/approval protocol plus protected native-provider implementations; deliberately separate from the general Rust validation/mutation protocol under Decision 0042.
matrix.permitted_delegation: The dedicated operator authorization and protected-service/confinement path remains authoritative. Rust assurance.snapshot is read-only and does not claim to enforce WI050 admission.
tests: Linux Landlock ABI 7 probe and platform pre-action conformance evidence
matrix.assurance_limit: Semantic/pre-action tests and Linux Landlock probe passed; installed production protected-service enforcement remains unverified as documented by RPS-012 evidence.

matrix.operation: Other explicitly unmigrated Core operations (spec, fleet/release orchestration, evidence-record construction)
matrix.authoritative_implementation: The Python Core command/module named by Decision 0042 or the specific verification contract.
matrix.permitted_delegation: They do not implement a second canonical validator; where repository validity or derived dashboard generation is part of the operation, they delegate that result/projection to Rust.

workbench_read_only_boundary.source_boundary: Published Workbench Rust imports Core validation snapshots, GraphQueryEngine, Repository/Core APIs, and repopact_mutation plan/apply; Tauri commands are typed adapters and the React surface presents DTOs and lifecycle choices rather than applying governance rules.
workbench_read_only_boundary.unresolved_dependency_observation: The declared e15fbcfa revision is not currently retrievable from ForgeWireLabs/repopact-core (GitHub API returned 422 No commit found; Git fetch returned remote error not our ref). This does not reveal a competing semantic implementation, but it is an existing clean-clone/buildability risk that the next separately authorized Workbench slice must resolve. No Workbench file was changed.

version_identity.normalization: Packaging normalizes 3.1.3dev1 to 3.1.3.dev1; EngineClient.expected_product_version returns 3.1.3.dev1; semantic version comparison is equal.
version_identity.engine_protocol: repopact-engine v1; required validate/dashboard/work/graph capabilities present

supersedes_assessment: The earlier partial RPS-007 inventory remains immutable historical evidence of the initial ambiguity. This operation-by-operation review resolves that ambiguity using the operator's explicit direction and accepted Decisions 0042/0070; it is not a change to those decisions or a blanket narrowing of RPS-007.
